walkthroughs.body_html:
The big formula:

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

If you run 100 m in 20 s, your speed = 100 ÷ 20 = 5 m/s.

You can rearrange the formula too:

Distance = Speed × Time
Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Common speed units:

m/s - science standard.
km/h - car speed limits in most countries.
mph - used in UK and USA roads.

Roughly: 1 m/s ≈ 3.6 km/h.

So 10 m/s = 36 km/h - the speed of a fast sprinter.

Real journeys aren't constant speed - you stop at lights, slow down for corners.

Average speed = total distance / total time.

Drive 60 km in 1.5 hours: average = 40 km/h, even if you sometimes went 70 or 0.

That's the value that shows up on satnavs as your overall trip speed.

mcqs.q: Why does a metal spoon in hot water heat up faster than a wooden one?
options: Charge was created by friction and pulled the balloon to the wall.
Metal heats up faster because it has more thermal energy to begin with.
Metal heats up faster because it has a lower specific heat capacity, requiring less energy per degree.
Metals have higher thermal conductivity, so heat is transferred more rapidly through them.
